chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār narrated from Abū ʿAlī ibn Rāshid, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: What do you say about furs—which of them may one perform salat in? He said: Which furs? I said: al-fanak, al-sinjāb, and al-sammūr. He said: So perform salat in al-fanak and al-sinjāb; but as for al-sammūr, do not perform salat in it. I said: And foxes—may one perform salat in them? He said: No, but they may be worn after the salat. I said: May I perform salat in the garment that is directly against it? He said: No.

key_terms.الثَّعَالِبُ: foxes, whose fur is ruled not to be used in salat
key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment or clothing layer being asked about
key_terms.السَّمُّورَ: sable or sammur fur, prohibited here for salat
key_terms.السِّنْجَابَ: squirrel fur, permitted here for salat
key_terms.الْفَنَكَ: a type of fur deemed permissible here for salat
key_terms.الْفِرَاءِ: fur garments or pelts under discussion for use in salat
key_terms.يَلِيهِ: that which is directly adjacent to or touching it
key_terms.يُصَلَّى: to have salat performed in or while wearing something

ai.seo_question: Which animal furs are permissible to wear during salat according to Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on performing salat in garments made from certain furs. It distinguishes between types of fur, permitting salat in al-fanak and al-sinjāb, while prohibiting it in al-sammūr and fox fur, and also disallowing prayer in a garment directly touching such material.
